generatedCover.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: editorial cover illustration for Brain Fog, a visual essay about the history of automation and economics.
Primary request: a sophisticated analog cut-paper collage connecting industrial-era machinery and the modern automated world. A large antique engraved metal flywheel and belt-driven steam engine on the lower left, a black and white vintage human hand extended from right toward a smaller articulated chrome robotic hand in the center, a small factory with smokestacks at lower center, and a tiny black silhouette of a worker standing in the foreground. Behind the objects, one large flat burnt-orange circle, like a sun. Fine sketchy dotted orbit lines and a few small star marks suggest curiosity. Quiet warm ivory paper background that blends into hex #f5f3eb. Black and white halftone engravings with very restrained muted orange accents. A thoughtful independent print magazine, beautiful tactile grain, playful but intellectual, intentional coherent collage with lots of breathing room around edges. Landscape 3:2 composition; all objects contained within frame; orange circle slightly right of center; high contrast cutouts, no rectangular photo borders. Not photorealistic, not 3D. No words, text, letters, numbers, watermarks, logos, gradients, or brain anatomy.
generatedCover.description: AI-generated editorial illustration. Not a historical photograph.

generatedInlineIllustration.description: AI-generated conceptual illustration of saved time and curiosity, not an archival photograph or scientific diagram.
generatedInlineIllustration.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: inline editorial illustration for a long-form essay about automation, saved working time, and freedom to explore.
Primary request: depict the moment when time freed by a machine becomes room for human curiosity. A quietly seated person at a desk with an open notebook, a small mechanical gear and an hourglass, looking through a wide window into a night sky with constellations. The sky subtly flows into the notebook as a visual metaphor for an open question.
Style/medium: textured paper collage and fine engraved linework, sophisticated literary magazine illustration, matching a site with warm ivory paper, charcoal ink and muted burnt orange accents.
Composition/framing: landscape 3:2, one coherent scene with generous open space, readable at small widths.
Constraints: no text, no letters, no logos, no watermark; conceptual illustration rather than an archival photograph or a scientific diagram.
